ai.description: This snake reaches 25–30 cm. It is dark brown above with yellow-spotted sides and a pale venter. A key feature is the small, flat, shield-like tail tip with a terminal scale. Family: Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis dindigalensis* is best distinguished by its unique, strongly bicarinate (two-keeled) terminal shield, which lacks the distinct spine found in many other species.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis dindigalensis* inhabits the moist, leaf-littered floors of evergreen and shola forests within the Sirumalai Hills at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Uropeltis dindigalensis* is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours burrowing through loose soil in search of earthworms and other small subterranean invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis dindigalensis* is viviparous, producing small litters of live young. While specific breeding data is limited, they likely reproduce during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis dindigalensis* is endemic to the Sirumalai Hills in the Western Ghats of Tamil Nadu, India, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
